top_story: Israeli policy discourse and violence against Palestinians intensified in parallel over the past two days, as a push for US backing to expel Gaza’s population was followed by Itamar Ben-Gvir publicly framing the removal of roughly 2 million Palestinians as a concrete objective. In the West Bank, that rhetoric aligns with worsening facts on the ground: 2026 has already become the deadliest year in recent memory, and repeated settler raids on one village this week culminated in Israeli forces shooting Palestinians, underscoring how settler action and state force are operating in tandem. The region’s conflict picture also darkened in Yemen on 4 September, where a major Houthi offensive toward a strategic Red Sea gateway triggered the country’s worst clashes in years and killed more than 120 people. The broader trajectory is one of hardening coercive agendas and rising civilian exposure, with local violence increasingly embedded in wider political projects rather than contained as isolated flare-ups.
